content:
I've just opened mathlib4#36813, which adds self-delimiting unary and pair encodings to Computability.Encoding.

This is a natural follow-up to my recent Primrec PR (mathlib4#36473) — now that we have the recursive proofs for takeWhile and drop, we can actually use them for a clean $1^n 0$ prefix-free encoding and pair pairing.

The injectivity proof for prefixPair turned out quite aesthetic thanks to a new cancellation lemma. I'd love to get some feedback :)

@Miyahara Kō reviewed this PR and pointed out a structural limitation: Encoding currently bundles its alphabet Γ.

To properly implement a strictly binary pair encoding, we can't use the existing finEncodingPair because it inflates the alphabet using a sum type (ea.Γ ⊕ eb.Γ). We need to be able to explicitly specify an Encoding α Bool. Beyond my PR, an unbundled Γ is also a prerequisite for formalizing Information Theory (Shannon) or Coding Theory (error-correcting codes), where the alphabet's size or algebraic structure must remain strictly fixed.
Proposal:

Unbundle Γ from the structure and make it a parameter:

structure Encoding (α : Type u) (Γ : Type v) where
  encode : α → List Γ
  decode : List Γ → Option α
  decode_encode : ∀ x, decode (encode x) = some x

To preserve encapsulation for abstract computability proofs (where the exact alphabet doesn't matter), we can simultaneously provide a bundled fallback via a Sigma type:

abbrev AnyEncoding (α : Type u) := Σ (Γ : Type), Encoding α Γ

This is a breaking change for Computability.Encoding (e.g., FinEncoding will need to extend Encoding α Γ). Since this affects the core structure, @Miyahara Kō suggested asking for consensus here.
I think this proposal should be posted as a new topic in #mathlib4 channel.
